items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.author: Aeri UI
items.description: A semantic Button with restrained press feedback.
items.docs:
## Purpose

Use Button for a discrete action. Use `default` for primary actions, `secondary` for lower emphasis actions, and `destructive` for irreversible actions. It inherits the Consumer Theme rather than applying an Aeri UI theme.

## Installation

Install with the Aeri UI registry command shown on this Item Page. Preview installations configure the Aeri UI registry URL in `components.json`.

## API and anatomy

`Button` accepts Base UI Button props, `className`, and the semantic `variant` prop. `variant` defaults to `default` and also accepts `secondary` and `destructive`. Set `pending` while asynchronous work is in progress to disable repeated activation, expose busy state, and show a native CSS progress indicator. Set `pendingText` to localized pending feedback. Button forwards its ref and renders one Base UI Button primitive. It exposes no raw motion controls.

## Dependencies and client boundary

`@base-ui/react` is Button's only runtime dependency. Button reaches Base UI's client boundary, so using it adds that client component to a Consumer Project. The Catalog Live Preview adds further client state only to expose controls.

## Accessibility

The Base UI primitive preserves native button semantics, Enter and Space activation, visible keyboard focus, disabled behavior, and form support. While `pending`, Button is disabled and exposes `aria-busy`; provide `pendingText` whenever the default label would not clearly communicate the pending action.

## Motion and performance

Press feedback uses CSS transform and color transitions. Pending feedback uses a CSS spinner only while work is pending, then stops completely. `prefers-reduced-motion` removes nonessential transitions and the spinner. There is no motion runtime, recurring idle timer, or animation frame loop.

## Consumer Theme

Button uses Consumer Theme semantic colors, typography, and radius. Override tokens in the Consumer Project and use `className` for local layout changes. The source does not add a global stylesheet or rewrite global tokens.

## Responsive, localization, and RTL

Button has no fixed width and reflows with its container. Its action label and `pendingText` are supplied by the Builder, so they can be localized. It inherits text direction from the Consumer Project and uses no directional motion.

## Compatibility

Button supports Next.js 16 App Router Consumer Projects using React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn, and Base UI. It works in light and dark Consumer Theme appearances and remains functional offline after installation.

items.name: accordion
items.title: Accordion
items.author: Aeri UI
items.description: Accessible disclosure content with measured, restrained expansion.

preview.label: Accordion preview
preview.interaction: Expand a question to reveal its answer

meta.example:
import { Accordion, AccordionHeader, AccordionItem, AccordionPanel, AccordionTrigger } from "@/components/aeri/accordion";

<Accordion defaultValue={["shipping"]}>
  <AccordionItem value="shipping">
    <AccordionHeader>
      <AccordionTrigger>When will my order arrive?</AccordionTrigger>
    </AccordionHeader>
    <AccordionPanel>Most orders arrive in three to five business days.</AccordionPanel>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>

items.docs:
## Purpose

Use Accordion to progressively disclose related content, such as FAQs, settings explanations, or supporting details. Use the default single expansion behavior when one answer should hold attention, or set `multiple` when Builders should compare several sections. It inherits the Consumer Theme rather than applying an Aeri UI theme.

## Installation

Install with the Aeri UI registry command shown on this Item Page. Preview installations configure the Aeri UI registry URL in `components.json`.

## API and anatomy

Compose `Accordion`, `AccordionItem`, `AccordionHeader`, `AccordionTrigger`, and `AccordionPanel`. Give every Item a stable string `value`. Accordion accepts Base UI Root props: `value`, `defaultValue`, and `onValueChange` support controlled or uncontrolled state, while `multiple` enables several open Items. Item accepts `disabled`. The parts forward their refs and preserve Base UI props. The API exposes no motion controls.

## Dependencies and client boundary

`@base-ui/react` is Accordion's only runtime dependency. Accordion reaches Base UI's client boundary, so using it adds that client component to a Consumer Project. The Catalog Live Preview adds further client state only to expose controls.

## Accessibility

Base UI supplies button triggers, headings, `aria-expanded`, panel relationships, regions, keyboard activation, visible focus, and disabled behavior. Provide concise Trigger labels and avoid using Accordion for content that must remain persistently visible.

## Motion and performance

The Panel uses Base UI's measured height variable for one short native CSS height transition. Height is necessary to reveal content without clipping or a layout jump. Reduced motion makes the change immediate. There is no motion runtime, recurring timer, or animation frame loop after the transition settles.

## Consumer Theme

Accordion uses Consumer Theme semantic colors, typography, and radius. Override tokens in the Consumer Project and use `className` for local layout changes. The source does not add a global stylesheet or rewrite global tokens.

## Responsive, localization, and RTL

Accordion has no fixed width and reflows with its container. Trigger and Panel content are supplied by the Builder, so they can be localized. It inherits text direction from the Consumer Project and uses a direction neutral disclosure indicator.

## Compatibility

Accordion supports Next.js 16 App Router Consumer Projects using React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn, and Base UI. It works in light and dark Consumer Theme appearances and remains functional offline after installation.
